messages:
sara: quick heads-up — I pushed samplevault-v1 embeddings (int8 per-channel quant) to staging catalog a few mins ago. running the usual recall/cluster sanity and seeing a regression on recall@10 vs float32 baseline (~6% drop). :thinking:

jin: can you paste the exact metrics and the eval command you ran? which test split?

sara: ran against holdout-10k (longtail queries). command:```python eval_embeds.py --model samplevault-v1 --quant int8 --dataset holdout-10k --metrics recall@1,5,10,umap``` results snippet:```baseline float32 -> recall@1: 0.328 recall@5: 0.612 recall@10: 0.722samplevault int8  -> recall@1: 0.322 recall@5: 0.588 recall@10: 0.662``` so recall@10 delta = -0.06 absolute (~8.3% relative).

jin: hmm recall@1 small but k10 drop is large. did you use same normalization and whitening pipeline? any change in PCA dim or whitening scaler?

sara: no pipeline changes. I re-ran with and without whitening:```with whitening recall@10: 0.662 without whiten recall@10: 0.665``` so whitening not the main culprit.

mike: infra note — the int8 build used the new GEMM kernel fallback on some machines (kernel v2.1). could that affect numeric stability for long vectors? cc @leo

leo: possible. can you run quick per-sample cos sims between float32 and int8 for the top-mismatch set? small script:```python compare_sims.py --float path/to/float/embs.npy --int8 path/to/int8/embs.npy --top-k 50 --out mismatches.csv```

sara: did that — attached top 50 mismatch pairs (pasted first 5):```q42: float_top1=doc314 (0.842), int8_top1=doc789 (0.611)q87: float_top1=doc22  (0.799), int8_top1=doc22  (0.602)q490: float_top1=doc902 (0.721), int8_top1=doc143 (0.518)q3: float_top1=doc7   (0.915), int8_top1=doc7   (0.706)q110: float_top1=doc400 (0.632), int8_top1=doc559 (0.431)``` lots of magnitude compression on the int8 side, distances shrunk and order flips.

jin: that suggests quantization scale/zero-point mismatch or per-channel scale variance. which quantization method did you use? symmetric per-channel?

sara: used symmetric per-channel with 8-bit dynamic range computed from calibration set (1000 samples).

leo: try per-tensor scale + bias correction trick (we've seen this help for some open models). also check whether we used the same normalization before quant step (L2).

 tara: I plotted UMAP of embeddings for a small category slice — float clusters are tight, int8 clusters are smeared and some centroids moved. link: https://console.redwood.ai/embeds/compare/samplevault-v1/umap (staging)

mike: can we reproduce quant using the older quant toolchain (v0.9) vs new (v1.2) to narrow whether it's quantizer or kernel? I can spin up both runners.

ops-bot: deploy event recorded — samplevault-v1 (int8) applied to staging catalog by sara at 2026-03-21T12:05:10Z :white_check_mark:

 sara: thanks — i'll re-run cal set at 10k samples instead of 1k, try per-tensor + bias correction, and also produce per-dim scale hist to see if any dims blow up. putting a small checklist: 1) re-calibrate with 10k 2) per-tensor quant 3) reproduce on kernel v0.9 4) per-dim sim diff export. pinging @mike for infra runs. :+1:

mike: on it — I'll queue 2 runs (v0.9 quant tool and v1.2) on a small fleet. ETA ~30m.

jin: if per-tensor helps, we may need to add quant-safety gating to rollout (auto-fallback to float for affected customers). file a quick RFC?

sara: filing a tiny RFC now -> https://docs.redwood.ai/rfcs/brief-quant-safety (draft).

leo: also recommend adding a small embedding consistency check in the pipeline (compare top-1 overlap > 95% on calibration set) as a rollout gate.

tara: agree. for tracking — created a ticket: #ENGML-8134 to track follow-ups and patch.

 sara: follow-ups done: re-cal with 10k produced recall@10 0.683 (delta -0.039), per-tensor bumped to 0.701 (delta -0.021), kernel v0.9 run similar to v1.2. conclusion: quantizer params (per-channel + small cal) caused most of the drop. will prepare PR to adopt per-tensor/bias-correct default for samplevault and add consistency gate. thanks team :raised_hands:
